answer: Shared-Vertex Attestation Relay. Each new agent must land on a unique vertex in a sparse routing graph, chosen so its neighborhood overlaps no existing identity's neighborhood by more than a fixed threshold. A periodic beacon broadcast collects each agent's neighbor set; duplicated agents show up as overlapping closures, since one operator cannot cheaply fake disjoint neighborhoods. To evade, an attacker must grow genuinely distinct neighbor sets, paying the full connectivity cost per duplicate rather than cloning a comet-like tail of shared links.
